title: From Vectors to Attention: the Mathematics Behind LLMs
summary: A mathematical map of an LLM: vectors represent tokens, matrices transform them, dot products compare them, softmax turns scores into weights or probabilities, and repeated Transformer blocks build contextual representations.
eli5: An LLM repeatedly turns words into lists of numbers, mixes those numbers according to what is relevant, and finally converts the resulting scores into probabilities for the next token.

sections.heading: The mathematical chain
items: A token is mapped to an embedding vector.
Learned matrices project vectors into new representations.
Dot products measure compatibility between vectors.
Softmax converts arbitrary scores into positive weights that sum to one.
Attention forms weighted mixtures of value vectors.
Feed-forward layers transform each token representation further.
After many blocks, a final linear map produces vocabulary logits and softmax can turn them into next-token probabilities.

sections.heading: Vectors and dot products
sections.explanation: A dot product collapses two equal-length vectors into one scalar. In attention, a scaled dot product is used as a compatibility score between a query and a key.
sections.shapes: If x and y are length d, x · y is a scalar.

sections.heading: Tiny dot-product example
steps: The dot-product score is therefore 2. A larger score can mean stronger compatibility, but its interpretation depends on how the vectors were learned.

sections.heading: Matrix multiplication is learned mixing
sections.explanation: A learned weight matrix W recombines the coordinates of x. Most neural-network layers are built from matrix operations plus nonlinear or normalization operations.
sections.shapes: If x is 1×d and W is d×m, h is 1×m.

sections.heading: From logits to probabilities
sections.explanation: Logits are unrestricted scores. Softmax exponentiates and normalizes them, producing non-negative values that sum to one. The same operation appears in attention weights and next-token probability distributions.

sections.heading: Two-logit softmax
sections.intro: Suppose the model has two scores, z = [2, 1].

sections.heading: Embeddings are learned coordinates
sections.body: An embedding assigns each token a dense vector. The individual coordinates usually do not have simple human labels; useful structure emerges from how the model learns to place and transform vectors so that later layers can exploit statistical relationships.

sections.heading: The core attention equation
sections.explanation: Queries are compared with keys, the scores are scaled and normalized, and those weights mix the value vectors. In self-attention, Q, K and V are projections of the same sequence representations.

sections.heading: A useful correction
sections.body: Saying that an LLM 'only predicts the next token' correctly describes its autoregressive training/generation objective at a high level, but it does not describe the internal computation. The prediction is produced by many layers of learned vector transformations and attention.

sections.heading: Check yourself
sections.question: Why is softmax useful in both attention and next-token prediction?
sections.answer: Because it converts a set of arbitrary scores into normalized positive weights. Attention uses those weights to mix value vectors; next-token prediction can interpret them as a probability distribution over vocabulary choices.
